critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1143 lines - still growing (documents + object storage plumbing added). Split into routers (auth, leads, calls, documents, chat) before the next feature to keep it maintainable.

storage.py uses the synchronous `requests` library while the rest of the backend is httpx/motor async - the run_in_threadpool wrapper is correct, but consider switching to httpx.AsyncClient for consistency and to reuse connection pooling.
storage.storage_key is a module-level global mutated without a lock; safe today because init_storage is idempotent, but flag for future concurrency work (e.g. multiple workers behind a shared cache).

upload_document reads the whole UploadFile into memory before checking size (file.read() then len check). For 15 MB max that is fine, but the 413 path only fires AFTER the entire body is buffered - consider a streaming size check or FastAPI file size middleware to reject early.
download_document swallows every storage exception into a generic 404 ('Document file not found') - a 502/503 with the underlying reason would be more diagnosable when the object store is degraded.
delete_document is a soft delete only (correct - object storage has no delete API), but there is no cleanup job / retention policy for stale is_deleted:true blobs; storage cost will grow unbounded.

Content-Disposition on the object-storage path is built with a naive f-string and no filename* fallback, so non-ASCII filenames will break. FileResponse (legacy branch) does this correctly - port the same logic to the object-storage branch.
call_attempts collection still has no TTL/index on created_at (flagged in iteration_3, not addressed).

success_rate.backend: 100% (105/105 pytest: 14 new documents + 20 smartflo + 71 pre-existing regression)
